title: registerFetcher
subtitle: Register a fetcher function for a query
description: Register a global fetcher function for a query key, allowing you to use the query without specifying a fetcher in each useQuery call.

rows.name: queryKey
rows.description: Unique identifier for the query. Can be a string or array of primitives.

rows.name: options
rows.description: Configuration object containing the fetcher function and optional settings.

rows.name: options.fetcher
rows.description: Function that returns a Promise resolving to the data.

rows.name: options.staleTime
rows.description: Time in milliseconds after which data is considered stale.

rows.name: options.refetchOnSubscribe
rows.description: When to refetch data when component subscribes.

examples.title: Basic Registration
examples.description: Register a fetcher for a query key

examples.title: With Options
examples.description: Register a fetcher with default options

behavior.title: Global Registration
behavior.description: Makes the fetcher available globally for the query key

behavior.title: Default Options
behavior.description: Sets default options that apply to all uses of the query

behavior.title: Simplified Usage
behavior.description: Allows useQuery calls without specifying a fetcher

behavior.title: Centralized Logic
behavior.description: Centralizes data fetching logic in one place

dos: Register fetchers early in your application lifecycle
Use descriptive query keys that match your API endpoints
Set appropriate default options for your use case
Keep fetcher functions pure and focused
donts: Don't register the same query key multiple times
Don't use complex logic in fetcher functions
Don't forget to handle errors in your fetchers
Don't register fetchers in render functions

callouts.title: Centralized Configuration
callouts.content: registerFetcher is perfect for centralizing your data fetching logic and configuration in one place.
